description: Composite figure group whose supplied pixels contain only a schematic diagram (identified by the caption as Fig. 9, "Schematic diagram of κ and (Ti, V) C of M2 steel"); the two EPMA panels the caption attributes to Fig. 8 are not present in the supplied image. The schematic is a before/after pair: two dark navy hexagonal domains, each labelled in the dashed legend box as "Austenite grain". The left hexagon (before aging) contains two circular (Ti, V)C carbide particles, each drawn as a concentric colour map running from a red core through orange/yellow and green to a blue rim, with the label "(Ti, V)C" and arrows pointing to both particles. A large black rightward arrow labelled "Aging at 550 °C" separates the two grains. The right hexagon (after aging) shows the same two (Ti, V)C carbides plus small grey rectangles labelled "κ", nucleated immediately alongside the carbides. The legend further defines open circle = (Ti, V)C carbide, grey rectangle = κ-carbide, and a red-to-blue colour bar = "The carbon content decreases along the arrow direction". No axes, numeric scales or scale bars are printed.

subfigures.description: Hexagonal austenite grain before aging, dark navy background, containing two circular (Ti, V)C carbide particles drawn with concentric carbon-content colour rings (red core → yellow/green → blue rim); label '(Ti, V)C' with two arrows points to the particles.
Large horizontal black arrow labelled 'Aging at 550 °C' pointing rightward from the un-aged hexagon to the aged hexagon, marking the aging treatment step.

Hexagonal austenite grain after aging at 550 °C, containing the same two (Ti, V)C carbides (still with red-core carbon gradient) plus several small grey rectangles labelled 'κ' located adjacent to the carbides; arrows from '(Ti, V)C' point to the two particles and an arrow from 'κ' points to the grey blocks.

Dashed-border legend box: hexagon = 'Austenite grain', open circle = '(Ti, V)C carbide', grey rectangle = 'κ-carbide', and a red-to-yellow-to-green-to-blue colour bar with arrow meaning 'The carbon content decreases along the arrow direction'.

observations.observation: The schematic shows two hexagonal domains, each identified in the legend as an 'Austenite grain', separated by a large rightward arrow labelled 'Aging at 550 °C'.

Each (Ti, V)C carbide particle is rendered as a concentric colour gradient with a red centre fading through orange/yellow and green to a blue rim, matching the legend colour bar where red denotes the highest and blue the lowest carbon content.

In the right-hand (aged) hexagon, small grey rectangles labelled 'κ' appear immediately adjacent to the (Ti, V)C carbide particles, whereas no such rectangles are present in the left-hand (before-aging) hexagon.

The legend defines the symbol mapping: hexagon = 'Austenite grain', open circle = '(Ti, V)C carbide', grey rectangle = 'κ-carbide', and states 'The carbon content decreases along the arrow direction' for the red-to-blue colour bar.
The only printed numeric value in the schematic is the aging temperature, 550 °C; there are no axes, gridlines, scale bars or magnification values.
The supplied image contains no EPMA elemental map panel, even though the caption describes Fig. 8 as 'EPMA images of M2-SS: (a) mapping domain, (b) C distribution around the (Ti, V)C carbides'.
The caption states Fig. 8 shows EPMA images of M2-SS: (a) mapping domain, (b) C distribution around the (Ti, V)C carbides, and that Fig. 9 is a schematic diagram of κ and (Ti, V) C of M2 steel.

The citing text asserts that, as shown in Fig. 8, carbon is enriched at the centre of (Ti, V)C carbides and decreases gradually toward the edges, with a surrounding carbon-rich region exceeding the matrix content; the schematic confirms only the centre-to-edge decrease, not a surrounding carbon-rich region.

The citing text states that the addition of Ti and V promotes precipitation of (Ti, V)C carbides before aging, which modulates the residual carbon concentration in the matrix, motivating the pre-aging state shown in the left hexagon.

The citing text describes M1 and M2 as having identical Mn and Al concentrations but different κ-carbide precipitation behaviour (homogeneous in M1, heterogeneous in M2 after aging), and identifies carbon as the predominant factor controlling κ-carbide precipitation sites.
